# 0.15.152

**The phone, rebuilt to the prototype.**

The Android interface is now the HTML prototype, followed exactly and then taken further
with what the recording of Discord's own phone showed: a drawer of spaces and messages underneath,
the conversation sliding over it and following your finger; screens that push in from the right
and pop back; sheets that rise with a little spring and are dragged away by their handle; a call
that fills the screen, slides back down with a swipe, and lives on as a floating tile you can drag
to any edge; what you send rising into place; a reaction that pops; every button giving under the
finger. The words are the desktop's wherever the desktop has them — Account, Identity & backup,
Devices, Privacy & safety, Notifications; Reply, Forward, Pin, Delete; Messages disappear after…;
Clear on this device.

**No more toasts.** Nothing floats over the page to tell you something. A copy button says
"Copied" on itself; a switch that could not be saved says so on its own row and shows what is
true; something that cannot be done says why in a box that needs an answer; a message the
application has for you sits in a line under the header until you dismiss it.

Also on the phone now: search over everything on the device (recent, people, media, pins, links,
files, with `from:` `has:` `before:` filters), a notifications screen for what is waiting on you,
threads, polls, posts channels, forwarding, per-conversation notification levels, pin to top,
nickname, relay-only, ignore, the space's settings pages (channels, members, roles, bans, history),
the phone's own appearance (mode, theme, accent, text size, pictures, layout, reduced motion),
a microphone test, the recovery file, and voice messages.

Desktop: one fix, in the code both interfaces share. When a panel was redrawn with its rows in a
different order — a settings page switching tabs, a list that gained a row in the middle — the
redraw could keep a stray element from the old version and drop the last one of the new. Found on
the phone (a channel's Permissions tab ending in a lone "Name" label); fixed for both.
